text:
aisha: quick thread — ran into a customer bug in private deployments where service-to-service requests leak project_id in auth claims across proxy hops

matt: ugh. example?

aisha: svc A in project-alpha calls shared proxy -> calls svc B in project-beta. proxy adds original_claims.project_id=alpha to outgoing token. svc B logs alpha in audit events and treats it as origin for RBAC checks. customer noticed cross-project visibility.

jun: is the proxy minting a new token or forwarding the original?

aisha: it mints a new token with an extra claim: orig_proj:alpha. so B sees both proj:beta (aud) and orig_proj:alpha

olivia: two immediate concerns: 1) leak of project mapping in telemetry/audit 2) authorization ambiguity when policies look at orig_proj vs aud

matt: behavior differs by environment. Hosted API strips orig_proj. Private VPC installs keep it by default for debugging. that's probably the root cause.

jun: tradeoff: keep orig_proj for traceability vs enforce strict containment. For RBAC decisions, we should only use the minted token's subject/audience claims. orig_proj must be treated as metadata, never as authz input.

aisha: agreed on principle. but we need migration and enforcement paths — can't break existing customer integrations that accidentally relied on orig_proj.

olivia: proposal: 3-phase plan — 1) telemetry-only: vendor logs show orig_proj presence with a "do-not-use-for-auth" tag in payloads; 2) enforce at middleware: drop orig_proj for any policy evaluation unless feature flag enabled; 3) remove entirely after TTL and communicate in release notes.
matt: +1. add runtime enforcement in runtime-config so Dedicated customers can opt into dropping now. Private deployments get a default to drop starting next major unless opt-out.
jun: how do we enforce at policy level? We could extend the policy language to reference claim_source("aud") vs claim_source("orig"). That avoids implicit use.
aisha: that requires changes across our RBAC engine, evaluation and policy UI. fairly large. alternative: runtime rewrite: rename orig_proj to orig_proj_meta and blacklist any policy referencing keys with _meta suffix. simpler but hacky.
olivia: hacky but low lift. long term we should do the explicit claim_source in policy language. short term rename + lint check across policies.
matt: add a scanner that flags policies referencing orig_proj (exact key) and open PRs to owners. also add regression alert if any production auth decisions start using orig_proj.
sec-ci-bot: security-scan: flagged 12 policies referencing "orig_proj". see https://ci.internal/scan/1757770000
jun: we should also consider operator workflows: support an "act-as" header for audit-only delegation so proxies can include origin without embedding in token claims used for authz.
aisha: suggested header: X-Orig-Act-As: svc/alpha (audit-only). proxies can forward as header, auth middleware ignores headers for auth decisions but logs them.
olm: (typo) meant olivia: need to ensure header propagation doesn't create header injection attack surface. sign headers with proxy key (HMAC) so downstream can verify provenance.
matt: implementable: proxy signs X-Orig-Act-As and X-Orig-Signature. middleware verifies via proxy cert public key store.
jun: action items: 1) a short RFC for claim visibility and migration plan (jun) 2) runtime feature flag + config defaults for Dedicated/Private (matt) 3) policy scanner + lint + auto-PR for flagged policies (aisha) 4) add header spec + signed-header verify in middleware (olivia)
aisha: timeline?
matt: can do scanner + flag in 2 weeks, header verify + HMAC in 3 weeks, RFC this week.
jun: I'll draft RFC today and include examples for policy language change.
aisha: thanks — please cc security on RFC. we'll triage flagged policies and coordinate with customers before enforcement. :thumbsup:

olivia: also add an observability metric: auth_decision_source where we tag whether decision used aud vs orig_proj. that will help measure impact before enforcement.
aisha: good call. sec-ci-bot, please open ticket to track metrics: AUTH-4286

sec-ci-bot: created ticket AUTH-4286 — https://tickets.internal/AUTH-4286

matt: ok, wrapping up. next check-in after RFC review. if anyone sees customers relying on orig_proj for admin flows ping me directly.
aisha: noted. thanks everyone.
